raw: The Fiery Star was a tea clipper, and on 21 June 1866 she cleared Foochow carrying 1,207 chests of tea destined for London. At the time of her departure she was drawing 19 feet of water. The ship belonged to George Thompson of Aberdeen, who that season had fitted her with Green's patent topsail yards. Her fastest day of the voyage produced a run of 328 miles, a distance recorded in her log on 30 June while she was in the China Sea. She anchored at Anjer on 8 July, where she took aboard 11 tons of coal along with fresh provisions, and she resumed her voyage the same evening. The full passage from Foochow to the Lizard lasted 89 days, with the ship arriving on 18 September. This put her six days behind the Serica, the vessel that carried the first tea of the season to market. When the Fiery Star's cargo was sold, it fetched an average price of two shillings and ninepence per pound. The ship sailed with a crew of 33 hands, four of whom were apprentices. One of these apprentices, David Bruce, kept a log of the voyage, and that log was later deposited at the Aberdeen Maritime Museum.

raw:
A dispatch from Broken Hill, dated 15 September 1893, conveyed news from a mining company called Silver Queen Proprietary. It reported that the company's new shaft had struck the lode at a depth of 340 feet, eleven weeks after work on sinking the shaft had begun on 1 July. An assay taken from the first crosscut showed a return of 22 ounces of silver to the ton across a width of 4 feet.

The company's workforce consisted of 87 men working underground and 44 men employed on the surface. The mine was run under the management of Daniel Callaghan, who had arrived from Kalgoorlie in April of that year.

On the surface, two winding engines, each rated at 60 indicated horsepower, had already been erected. A third engine had been ordered from Mort's Foundry in Sydney at a price of 1,850 pounds.

Water was coming into the bottom of the shaft at a rate of 900 gallons per hour, and this inflow was being dealt with by a Cornish pump.

The dispatch also recorded two further items: wages had been increased by two shillings per shift as a result of the strike that took place in August, and the amalgam retorts had produced 3,100 ounces of silver for the month.
